findings.title: full-logit CUDA parity and compatible transforms are incomplete
findings.resolution: The 2026-08-15 accepted-prefix divergence was downstream of a pre-proposal installed DFlash-context mismatch, not transport, layout, rollback, or trace accounting. The Mac draft Q/K head norms hardcoded epsilon 1e-6 while the pinned GGUF and llama.cpp producer used 1e-5; the CUDA draft rope also used stock transcendental construction instead of the strict fixed-point NCO route after token 0. Commit f778697 and the pinned Spark NCO adapter corrected both transforms. The fixed one-cell diagnostic and subsequent three-repetition campaign matched target tokens/full logits, final tokens, raw proposal and accepted traces, every accepted-prefix count, and the complete DFlash context bit-for-bit. The native NVFP4 product lane continues to reject DFlash by contract.
evidence_notes: 2026-08-15: retained strict 1x evidence passed exact target tokens/full logits and exact final target/local/remote tokens, but canonical offline diff proved a semantic accepted-prefix-count divergence; raw proposal arrays were not retained. The later retained v3 trace fixes the label direction: the qualifier's local counts are [1,0,4,6,...] and remote counts are [1,2,4,7,...], so the first differing round (zero-based index 1) is local=0 and remote=2. The opposite local=2/remote=0 sentence in docs/gx-speculative-trace-offline-20260815.md is a historical label reversal, not evidence used for closure.

2026-08-15/16 root cause: the retained v3 cell differed before proposal generation at layer 0 key token 0 element 0 (local 0x3ea8f873, remote 0x3ea8f85f), proving an installed-state problem. The bit signature and offline head-mean probe isolate the 1e-6 versus 1e-5 head-norm epsilon, with a second latent stock-rope versus NCO mismatch. Evidence: muser-receipt://gx10-dflash-trace-context-v3/20260815T204217Z-85211415c5cc47c4851477f94541b9e3.command.log and muser-receipt://20260816T012001Z-220fa93f49f14d01b1b0e34fa9db3998.command.log.

findings.title: global single Session mutex instead of four isolated resident slots
findings.resolution: Replaced the global Session lease with a bounded 1..=4 resident SlotPool; each slot has independent target and DFlash state, admission is capped at 64 waiters, and poison latches inference unavailable until restart.

findings.title: multi-sequence kernels, decode-first scheduling, and bounded queue absent
findings.resolution: Implemented a rotating decode-first scheduler, bounded 64-request admission, four isolated resident slots, and a continuous decode rendezvous that submits up to four ready rows together. Exact multi-column Q4_K/Q5_K kernels share each weight load while preserving pinned single-row arithmetic; Q6_K retains adjacent pinned matvec rows. A real pinned-model four-row differential passes bit-for-bit full logits, exact selected tokens, every target KV row, and unequal per-slot positions; four concurrent public completion requests exercise all slots and Prometheus records packed submissions.

findings.title: terminal emitted token is not always consumed before revision commit
findings.resolution: Target-only decode consumes every selected non-EOS token before stop or length completion, including the final visible token.

findings.title: target DFlash sampler logits and visible frontier combined commit is absent
findings.resolution: Greedy and sampled verification commit only the exact target-accepted prefix; known terminal candidates are cut before target submission, target logits/hidden state advance together, and publication callbacks run only after that combined frontier commits. Text-stop requests remain target-only.

findings.title: DFlash emits a completed vector instead of incremental verified-prefix callbacks
findings.resolution: DFlash invokes a verified-prefix callback after every committed round; SSE and NDJSON publish those prefixes immediately through bounded writers, and any engine failure after publication latches accelerator health instead of falling back behind the stream.

findings.title: encrypted complete session bundles and canonical session API absent
findings.resolution: Implemented the canonical session CRUD/save/restore routes, 64-session revision-CAS admission, idempotent mutation replay, and authenticated XChaCha20-Poly1305/Postcard bundles. Each validated bundle binds model/tokenizer/template/layout identity; exact target KV, logits and token witnesses; DFlash context; RNG seed and sampler history; detokenizer/stop/grammar boundary state; canonical replay messages; context epoch/revision; and projected vision rows. Stateful DFlash and vision requests now retain those states, exact restored prompt cuts reuse cached logits, and encrypted restart/tamper tests cover complete DFlash plus vision material.

findings.title: transactional decode-node and storage-tier migration absent
findings.resolution: Added resumable two-phase decode migration over authenticated platform-verified HTTPS and enrolled kvpack storage-tier copy/move over strict-known-host SSH. Transfers persist private fsync-backed journals; bind exact encrypted payload bytes/SHA-256, session and ABI identities; stream under a separate bounded body budget; stage and authenticate before durable destination publication; reconcile ambiguous ACKs idempotently; and delete the source only after destination commit. Storage restore commits locally before optional remote deletion. Tests cover complete copy/move, storage round-trip, duplicate commit/ACK loss, tamper, ABI mismatch, and injected write/file-fsync/rename/directory-fsync failures without partial logical publication.

findings.title: atomic canonical context shift policy absent
findings.resolution: The default shift policy now reserves the requested output, preserves all leading system messages, retains only whole newest user/assistant/tool/image turn units, and fails when the minimum retained unit cannot fit. Raw mode retains the configured exact prefix plus newest suffix. Shift rebuilds in a separately leased staging slot and revision-CAS publishes the new canonical replay cut only after generation succeeds; abort tests prove the previous revision and epoch remain intact on failure.

findings.title: frozen llama route and strict DTO parity incomplete
findings.resolution: Implemented every route in the frozen llama-server contract plus strict native/OpenAI/Ollama request validation, physical slot save/erase/restore, resumable SSE lookup/replay/delete, active reasoning control, and transport-level disconnect cancellation. The fail-closed 52-check live differential against llama.cpp 89e0aa6 passes exact template/token/stream/tool/sampler behavior, 2.86e-6 maximum logprob error, 0.99999999999999 embedding cosine with 1.49e-8 maximum error, exact three-position slot restore, byte-equivalent resumable replay, and active reasoning-end control.

findings.title: complete sampler order and route defaults incomplete
findings.resolution: Implemented source-pinned route defaults and ordered logit bias; repetition/presence/frequency and DRY penalties; top-n-sigma, top-k, typical-p, top-p, min-p, XTC; dynamic temperature; adaptive-p; Mirostat 1/2; MT19937 seed/RNG; grammar/EOS/stop handling; and deterministic target-distribution logprobs. Explicit sampler lists preserve client order, the default chain matches llama.cpp 89e0aa6, infill is rejected by contract, and grammar follows the pinned rejection/resampling path so the rejected draw and constrained redraw consume RNG exactly like the source.

findings.title: GBNF UTF-8 and JSON-schema parity incomplete
findings.resolution: Ported incremental UTF-8 GBNF matching with split-codepoint, inverse-class, ambiguity, repetition, and token-terminal coverage. Earley nullable closure now reaches a true fixed point, and the source-pinned JSON-schema converter uses llama.cpp's bounded space rule, preserves property order and array precedence, resolves object/array JSON pointers, implements anyOf/allOf/enum intersections and closed objects, validates unsupported constraints fail-closed, compiles bounded integers without expansion, and translates atom-aware regex repetitions, classes, groups, alternation and dot semantics. A live real-model schema differential matches visible JSON, every token including primary EOS, and target logprobs within 2.15e-6.

findings.title: Muse ATEM tool and reasoning parsing incomplete
findings.resolution: The actual GGUF template now receives strict tool definitions, tool-result messages, Python-compatible split and ordered JSON rendering, all none/auto/required/named tool_choice modes, and parallel_tool_calls. Incremental and final ATEM parsers preserve reasoning/content phases, validate recipient/function/parameter structure and JSON-schema arguments before socket emission, emit indexed delta.tool_calls, reject malformed or disallowed output, and never execute tools. The retained real-template fixture and live pinned llama.cpp differential produce the same 1,708 prompt bytes (SHA-256 f76d76d4b890c44c3c072577fbd5f16337e572454e3890a14a04a6adcf3e7075).

A live same-backend differential against llama.cpp 89e0aa6 passes token-prefix lengths 1 through 6 plus the retained Muse prompt: minimum cosine 0.999999885966 and maximum absolute error 0.000085745, inside the frozen 0.999999/0.0001 thresholds.

Scope remains exactly the measured synthetic and single-producer lanes.
